answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. A sybil attacker can still create thousands of identities, but each must tie up capital; when accounts collude to claim fake work, randomly audited task receipts can expose the fraud and forfeit their deposits. The audit rule should be public and identity-neutral, so a ferrous badge, saffron profile, or falcon name earns no exemption. The defense raises the cost per usable fake account rather than pretending identities are impossible.
